research_question: What is the effect of early (started before 7 days of postnatal age), low-dose systemic dexamethasone (cumulative dose below 2 mg/kg), compared with placebo or no treatment, on the combined outcome of death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) at 36 weeks' postmenstrual age in preterm infants at risk of BPD?
treatment_label: Early low-dose systemic dexamethasone (<2 mg/kg cumulative, initiated <7 days postnatal age)
outcome_description: Combined outcome of death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD, defined as oxygen requirement or chronic lung disease) at 36 weeks postmenstrual age, assessed among all randomised infants (intention-to-treat).
positive_direction: A reduction in the risk of death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia (RR < 1, favouring dexamethasone over control).
search_queries: preterm infants early low dose dexamethasone bronchopulmonary dysplasia randomized trial
neonatal systemic dexamethasone death chronic lung disease controlled trial
early dexamethasone preterm infant oxygen dependence 36 weeks trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials evaluating early systemic dexamethasone initiated before 7 days of postnatal age with a cumulative dose below 2 mg/kg compared to placebo or no treatment in preterm infants born before 37 weeks gestational age.
Studies reporting quantitative data on the combined outcome of death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia (chronic lung disease / oxygen requirement) at 36 weeks postmenstrual age.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, commentary, narrative reviews, conference abstracts without data, and study protocols are excluded).

No comparison between low-dose dexamethasone and a placebo or no-treatment control condition (e.g., trials comparing dexamethasone to another steroid or comparing two active steroid regimens without a placebo/untreated arm).

Cumulative dexamethasone dose of 2 mg/kg or more, initiation of dexamethasone at 7 days of life or later, or trials of non-systemic corticosteroids (inhaled/intratracheal) or other steroids (e.g., hydrocortisone alone).
No extractable quantitative data for death or BPD (chronic lung disease / oxygen dependence) at 36 weeks postmenstrual age.
moderators_to_extract: Mean or median gestational age / birth weight of enrolled infants
Blinding and study design quality (double-blind vs open-label)
effect_size_note: Risk ratio (RR) calculated for the combined outcome of death or BPD at 36 weeks postmenstrual age using the number of infants randomised as the denominator (intention-to-treat). If death and BPD in survivors are reported separately, events are summed. An RR < 1 indicates dexamethasone reduces the risk of death or BPD.
single_outcome_target: death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia at 36 weeks postmenstrual age
